topic: what the runtime does: Node's certificate store, and the mode a copied file gets
notes: Phase 0 could not search: this machine's egress reaches github.com, api.github.com, codeload and the npm registry, and the keyless search lane's provider is outside it (recorded in research/MAP.md). The three pages are therefore named directly - the runtime owner's own files at the tag of the runtime in use (v22.22.0). fs.md carries the overwrite default and the COPYFILE_* semantics; deps/uv/docs/src/fs.rst is the layer that performs the copy; doc/node.1 carries NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS whole, where the GitHub viewer truncates the 116 KB doc/api/cli.md before its environment-variable section. All three are plain GitHub pages, so a failed fetch would cost nothing but would show up in the ledger.

urls.why: U-02 (the copy overwrites an existing destination by default; COPYFILE_EXCL is what makes it fail) and U-01 (what the page does and does not say about the destination's permissions)
U-01, U-02: uv_fs_copyfile is the layer that performs the copy; its flags and its documented default decide what the deploy's second run does
U-03: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS - what it extends, the missing/malformed-file behaviour, and that it is read only at process launch
